title: Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes: TODAY Trial, Metformin, GLP-1 RAs and Microvascular Screening

steps.title: Aggressive Beta-Cell Demise in Youth-Onset T2D

vis.alt: Autoimmune beta cell loss in type 1 diabetes contrasted with insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.
vis.caption: Type 1 autoimmunity contrasted with type 2 insulin resistance. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The TODAY trial demonstrated that beta-cell function declines 3-4 times faster in youth-onset type 2 diabetes (20-35% annual decline) than in adult-onset T2D, leading to rapid oral therapy failure. Understanding **Aggressive beta-cell failure in pediatric T2D** demonstrates how severe pubertal insulin resistance and glucolipotoxicity drive rapid exhaustion of pancreatic insulin reserve. This hyper-accelerated decline necessitates prompt treatment intensification beyond simple lifestyle modifications.
steps.say: The TODAY study showed that pancreatic beta-cell function declines up to four times faster in youth than in adult-onset type two diabetes.

steps.title: Metformin First-Line Titration and Precautions

rows: Hold during acute dehydration, hypoxia, or sepsis

steps.tx: Oral metformin is initiated at 500-1000 mg daily and titrated to 2000 mg/day (divided BID) with meals; contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m² or during acute dehydration/hypoxia due to lactic acidosis risk. Guiding **Metformin first-line titration** shows how metformin suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis and activates AMP-activated protein kinase without inducing hypoglycemia. Gradual upward dose titration with meals minimizes gastrointestinal adverse effects such as nausea and diarrhea.
steps.say: Oral metformin is titrated to two thousand milligrams daily as first-line therapy, but must be held during dehydration due to lactic acidosis risk.

steps.title: Approved GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric T2D

left.title: Liraglutide Daily Injection
points: Approved in youth >= 10 years of age
Titrated from 0.6 mg up to 1.8 mg subcutaneously daily
Promotes satiety and slows gastric emptying

right.title: Once-Weekly Formulations
points: Significant reductions in HbA1c and body mass index

steps.tx: Subcutaneous GLP-1 receptor agonists liraglutide (up to 1.8 mg daily) and once-weekly dulaglutide (0.75-1.5 mg) or semaglutide are FDA-approved in youth >= 10 years, achieving significant HbA1c and BMI reductions. Leveraging **GLP-1 receptor agonist approvals in youth** utilizes incretin mimetics to augment glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release, and induce central satiety. These agents offer a potent non-insulin option to stabilize glycemic control and promote weight loss.
steps.say: Glucagon-like peptide one receptor agonists including liraglutide and weekly dulaglutide are approved for children aged ten and older.

steps.title: Insulin Initiation Thresholds at Initial Presentation

nodes.label:
Glycemic Thresholds
HbA1c >= 8.5% or glucose >= 250 mg/dL

Concurrent Metformin
Add oral metformin as acidosis clears

steps.tx: Basal insulin (glargine 0.25-0.5 U/kg/day) must be initiated alongside lifestyle and metformin if HbA1c >= 8.5%, blood glucose >= 250 mg/dL, ketosis, or metabolic decompensation is present at diagnosis. Adhering to **Insulin initiation criteria in new-onset youth** overcomes high initial glucose toxicity that suppresses endogenous insulin secretion. Once metabolic stability is achieved, insulin can frequently be tapered down if metformin and GLP-1 therapy succeed.
steps.say: Basal insulin is required at diagnosis when hemoglobin A1c reaches eight point five percent or blood glucose exceeds two hundred and fifty.

steps.title: Immediate Microvascular Complication Surveillance

right.title: Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes
points: Dilated funduscopy and fasting lipid panel

steps.tx: Unlike type 1 diabetes where screening begins after 5 years, pediatric T2D mandates screening for microalbuminuria (urine ACR >= 30 mcg/mg), diabetic retinopathy (dilated eye exam), and dyslipidemia immediately at diagnosis. Enforcing **Immediate microvascular complication screening** is critical because youth-onset type 2 diabetes has a prolonged subclinical phase, meaning end-organ pathology is frequently already established at presentation. Yearly surveillance ensures early intervention.
steps.say: Screening for microalbuminuria, retinopathy, and dyslipidemia must begin immediately at diagnosis in youth-onset type two diabetes.

steps.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis

vis.alt: Liver progression from simple steatosis through steatohepatitis to cirrhosis.
vis.caption: Fatty liver: steatosis progressing to cirrhosis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Screening for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH / MASLD) with serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is mandatory at diagnosis; ALT > 2x upper normal limit persistent for 6 months warrants pediatric GI evaluation. Implementing **NASH and liver fibrosis screening** recognizes that severe visceral adiposity and hepatic insulin resistance drive profound triglyceride accumulation and inflammatory fibrosis. Early evaluation detects progressive steatohepatitis before cirrhosis develops.
steps.say: Serum aminotransferase testing at diagnosis screens for steatohepatitis, where persistent two-fold elevations warrant specialist evaluation.

steps.title: Hypertension Detection and Renin-Angiotensin Blockade
steps.tx: Blood pressure >= 95th percentile or >= 130/80 mmHg in pediatric T2D is treated promptly with an ACE inhibitor enalapril or ARB losartan, monitoring for hyperkalemia and teratogenicity counseling in adolescent females. Protocol for **Hypertension screening and ACE inhibitor therapy** with enalapril or losartan slows renal glomerulosclerosis and reduces urinary albumin leakage. Because ACE inhibitors and ARBs are strictly teratogenic, mandatory contraception education is essential in adolescent females.
steps.say: Hypertension in young diabetics requires prompt angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor therapy, paired with strict teratogenicity precautions.

steps.title: Bariatric Metabolic Surgery in Severe Adolescent Obesity

rows: Lifelong multivitamin, iron, B12, vitamin D

steps.tx: Metabolic bariatric surgery (vertical sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y) is indicated in adolescents with BMI >= 35 kg/m² with severe comorbidities (poorly controlled T2D, severe sleep apnea) or BMI >= 40 kg/m². Adhering to **Bariatric metabolic surgery criteria in adolescents** restores endogenous insulin sensitivity through surgical alteration of gastrointestinal hormones, inducing complete diabetes remission in over 70-80% of adolescents. Lifelong nutritional micronutrient supplementation is essential.
steps.say: Metabolic surgery is indicated for severe adolescent obesity with poorly controlled diabetes, offering high rates of glycemic remission.
